Below is an essay you revised once. Revise it so that it reads as if a US grade 8 student wrote it in class for a timed writing test. Keep the position it argues and keep it at about 376 words. The file must contain only the revised essay.

Essay:

Dear Principal,

I think we should adopt Policy 1, which lets students bring phones to school and use them during lunch and other free time as long as the phones stay off during class. I know a full ban seems easier, but I do not think it fixes the real problem, and it creates new ones.

First, phones matter for more than games. A lot of students carry a phone so they can reach their parents if a bus gets canceled, if practice ends late, or if something happens at home. If Policy 2 passes, those students will not have a good way to contact anyone during the day, and the office will get flooded with people asking to pass messages along. Policy 1 keeps that connection open without getting in the way of learning.

Second, the no-phones-in-class rule already deals with the biggest worry. If phones are off during lessons, the distraction teachers complain about most is gone. Lunch and passing periods are supposed to be a break. A kid who scrolls on a phone at lunch is not really doing worse than a kid who plays chess or cards.

Third, a total ban would be hard to enforce. Students who are used to having phones will keep them in backpacks, hide them in their jackets, or use them in the bathroom where nobody is watching. Then teachers and staff spend their time taking phones away and arguing with students instead of helping them. A simple rule that students can actually follow is easier to enforce than a strict rule that everyone breaks.

Finally, Policy 1 teaches responsibility. Students learn to manage their own devices and turn them off when it is time to focus. That is a skill we will need in high school, in college, and at a job. If we ban phones completely, we never get the chance to practice it, and we are not ready for a world where phones are everywhere.

For these reasons, I think Policy 1 is the better choice. It keeps students connected, protects class time, is realistic to enforce, and helps us build self-control. I would be happy to help write the guidelines or talk with teachers about how it could work.

Respectfully,

A Concerned Student
